fills.explanation: Standard Kephalaia chapter opening formula introducing the topic; "Concerning the Light" = "Concerning Divine wisdom" in the spiritual reading.

"Mystery" (ⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ) is the standard Kephalaia term for hidden knowledge that is "unveiled"; "Light, the mystery which he has unveiled" is a natural Manichaean phrase pairing revelation with mystery.

Double-verb hendiadys ("unveiled and revealed") is standard Coptic rhetorical style, and "to" is grammatically required before "his disciples"; the spiritual reading confirms disclosure to those who receive instruction.
Standard Kephalaia construction after "revealed to his disciples" specifying the content revealed: "concerning the entire treasure of wisdom" introduces the topic of the unveiling.
"Treasure of wisdom" is a standard gnostic/Manichaean phrase corresponding to the fullness of interior understanding in the spiritual reading.

Creates a parallel listing structure: "concerning the entire treasure of wisdom, and concerning the word in the beginning, concerning the separation" — each topic of revelation introduced by the same formula.

The separation of Light from Darkness is THE central Manichaean doctrine; the spiritual reading confirms "separation of good from evil" and the text places this "in the heights" — the boundary between the two primordial realms.
The spiritual reading shows ascending movement from outer celestial states toward the inmost; "the heights up to the heights" describes this upward reach.
The spiritual reading specifies "wage spiritual combat against the divine dominion"; "make war against the kingdom" is the standard Kephalaia construction.

The Darkness's desire/coveting of the Light is THE fundamental Manichaean motive for the cosmic conflict; after spreading out to make war against the kingdom, the dark powers desired the Light in the heights — this is the narrative hinge of the entire cosmogony.
The Light in the heights is described as transcendent, separated from all the aeons; the spiritual reading indicates distinction from all successive states proceeding from the Divine.
The negative frame "no X in it" describing the purity of Light strongly constrains the fill; the spiritual reading confirms no falsity can exist within Divine wisdom.
The most common Kephalaia paragraph connector (ⲁⲩⲱ); ¶2 continues the cosmological enumeration begun in ¶1, adding the description of the Darkness realm alongside the Light.
Simple conjunction listing features of the Darkness: "the world and their root" names the dark realm and its origin as parallel attributes.
Resumptive pronoun common in Coptic Kephalaia style: "their root, the one which poured forth" identifies the root with a relative clause.
Simple conjunction linking parallel actions of the Darkness: "It spread a quarrel and it disturbed" follows the text's paratactic narrative style.
In the Manichaean narrative, the crisis of the Darkness's attack prompts a cry for divine help; the spiritual reading's "extremity of spiritual need" corresponds to this call in distress.
The First Man proceeds from the Father of Greatness in standard Manichaean cosmogony; the spiritual reading confirms a divine source from which the power proceeds.
The First Man puts on/clothes himself with the five light elements as armor; the spiritual reading confirms he assumed the protective truths of divine wisdom.
The armor of Light is deployed "against" all the enmity; the spiritual reading frames this as protective truths arrayed against the fundamental opposition of evil.
Confirming the editor's choice: "the enmity" correctly renders the essential antagonism between heavenly order and the hells identified in the spiritual reading.
Narrative temporal connector marking progression from the First Man's combat to the next phase of cosmic construction; standard Kephalaia transitional word.

The sun and moon are invariably paired in Manichaean cosmology as vessels of light recovery; the spiritual reading's "divine love" (sun) implies the complementary vessel (moon) transporting light to the aeons.

Standard Kephalaia narrative transition (ⲁⲩⲱ ⲙⲛⲛⲥⲁ ⲛⲁⲓ) marking the shift from the First Man's battle and rescue to the Living Spirit's creative ordering of the cosmos — a major phase transition in the cosmogonic sequence.
The Living Spirit "spread out the universe and the earth" — conjunction linking the two objects of the creative act; the spiritual reading pairs spiritual order with the external natural.

The Living Spirit's fundamental cosmogonic work is separating Light from Darkness; after spreading out the universe and earth, the next act is division of the two natures — the spiritual reading confirms the ordering of wisdom and falsity.
Parallel construction: "He stood firm and was fixed" — the spiritual reading says "established immovably," requiring a passive verb linking "stood firm" to "fixed."
Simple conjunction connecting the two clauses: "He constructed the foundation and all of it was set up"; the spiritual reading confirms sequential completion.

Parallel to the "underneath" clause; "above he established the three earths" describes the Living Spirit constructing the layered cosmic structure; the spiritual reading confirms three degrees of the natural mind being established.
Definite article preceding "four mountains": "He enclosed the earth in the four mountains and three vessels" — standard Kephalaia cosmographic description.
Conjunction extending the list of cosmic features: four mountains, three vessels, and the seas and mountains — all elements of the earth's enclosure described in the spiritual reading.

Relative clause connecting the cosmic features (seas, mountains) to the Living Spirit's ordering act: "which he set in order upon it" — the spiritual reading confirms arrangement upon the external natural.
The universe "stood firm as a bond for the evil powers" — the spiritual reading confirms the cosmos functions as a restraint; "as" is the only natural connector here.
Parallel structure: the universe is a bond for the evil powers AND for the light joined with Darkness; the spiritual reading confirms both evil and commingled wisdom are restrained.

Echoes the earlier "the Light and the Darkness in the beginning" from ¶5, creating thematic consistency; the light was joined with Darkness "in the beginning" — at the primordial mixing that necessitated the cosmos as a bond.
Confirming the editor's choice: the Third Ambassador's role is purifying the commingled light, and "purified" adequately encompasses the separation process described in the spiritual reading.
Confirming the editor's choice: "redeemer" precisely captures liberation from bondage to falsity as described in the spiritual reading, and fits the Third Ambassador's role of freeing captive light.
Causal connector introducing the explanation of why purification occurs: the Light and Darkness are mixed in all things throughout the universe, hence the fire of refinement.
Conjunction linking the consumption of evil to the fate of the Light: "it is devoured, and all the portion of the Light also" — the spiritual reading shows both processes occurring together.
"All the portion of the Light" is standard Manichaean terminology for light mixed in matter undergoing purification; the spiritual reading confirms this as the wisdom being refined.
The Darkness "goes out" in contrast to the Light which "goes up" — parallel directional verbs describing the final separation; the spiritual reading confirms the falsity is expelled outward.
Transitional conjunction shifting subject from the confined Darkness to the liberated Light elements who now "unveil" their glory; consistent with the spiritual reading's disclosure of wisdom.
The purified Light elements become perfume (spiritual fragrance) "and they are set up" (established) — leading naturally to "and they reign for ever"; the spiritual reading confirms establishment.

Standard Kephalaia eschatological repetition: "set up for ever, and they reign for ever" — the doubling of "for ever" is characteristic of Coptic Manichaean closing formulas emphasizing permanent restoration.

The eschatological climax: "a single God comes to be king over the totality" — the spiritual reading confirms sovereign dominion, and "king" echoes "the King of the Light" used later in the same sentence.
Standard Manichaean title pair: "the King of the Light and the aeons of the Light" — the Father's sovereignty encompasses both the Light itself and all its proceeding states (aeons).

Introduces the Manichaean three-times framework (past, present, future); the spiritual reading renders this as "the states in which they occur" — "times" is the natural-plane term for these cosmic periods.
Declarative connector (ϫⲉ) introducing the content clause: "from the beginning, that they are mixed" describes the cosmic state since the primordial conflict — Light and Darkness commingled.
Standard Kephalaia formula introducing a lesson's content: "The first great lesson concerns that which in the [sphere]" — directing attention to the cosmic structure described next.
The "twelve" and "walks/revolves" strongly constrain this to the celestial sphere; the Kephalaia uses "sphere" for the rotating zodiacal heavens through which the twelve signs progress.
The twelve zodiac signs within the celestial sphere; the spiritual reading renders these as "twelve completions of faith" — in the Kephalaia's natural vocabulary, these are the twelve signs.
The cities and dwelling places are found "in the world" — the spiritual reading's doctrinal systems and states of life exist within the general order of the natural world.
